title: Satish Chandra v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Sudhir Agarwal, J.; Kaushal Jayendra Thaker, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; petitioner relegated to clause 6.5.
headnote: A consumer disputing electricity bills and a demand notice of Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. was refused Article 226 interference and relegated to the statutory objection before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: Satish Chandra petitioned the Allahabad High Court against electricity bills and a demand notice issued by the Executive Engineer, Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd., Shikohabad, District Firozabad. He disputed the correctness of those charges. The State and the distribution company appeared. After hearing counsel, the Division Bench considered whether the billing dispute should be entertained in writ jurisdiction or left to the Supply Code machinery.

holding_units.holding: A consumer disputing the correctness of electricity bills and a demand notice has a statutory alternative remedy under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 by raising the dispute before the competent authority, and the High Court will not interfere under Article 226.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the electricity bills and demand notice
not_decided.note: Merits of the billing dispute were not examined; petitioner was relegated to Clause 6.5.
